body: Lumines: Electronic Symphony is Q Entertainment's PlayStation Vita puzzle game, first released in North America on 15 February 2012. Two-colour blocks fall onto a board where matching squares wait for a moving Time Line to clear them. Music and visual skins change the atmosphere while the same arrangement problem continues beneath them. The Vita edition develops the series around its electronic soundtrack and the handheld's display and controls. A long session becomes a sequence of changing moods, with the player learning to maintain a clear board while the sound and appearance move on around it.

The player rotates and places each block to assemble larger same-colour groups. Those groups remain until the Time Line reaches them, allowing a useful formation to grow before it is removed. The delay creates both opportunity and pressure: a larger clear may reward patience, but the next piece still needs somewhere to land. The Vita allows ordinary buttons and sticks as well as touch input, offering different ways to control the same decisions. Whatever the method, success depends on seeing how a small placement changes the board that will exist a few moments later.

Ubisoft announced the game in 2011, with early demonstrations featuring The Chemical Brothers and Kaskade. James Mielke produced the release, which reached PAL territories in February 2012 and Japan in April. The licensed electronic selection gives the familiar puzzle a particular identity, using changes in rhythm and atmosphere to make continued play feel like travelling through a curated set. The series' strength remains the connection between two timelines: the next block demands an immediate decision, while the music and sweeping line determine when the consequences of that decision become visible.
